newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African bond yields ended higher on Wednesday as the market tracked movements on the U.S. Treasury bond market, dealers said.
At 1414 GMT, the key R150 was pegged at a 15.55 percent yield compared with 15.02 percent after trading in a tight 15.10 to 15.165 percent range for much of the day.

Dealers said the market's gains at the start of this week were eroded after the U.S. Treasury bond market moved contrary to expectations after the U.S. Federal Reserve hiked U.S. interest rates by 25 basis points.
"People were expecting that with the 25-point rate hike, the U.S. would strengthen," a trader said, adding that perceptions were that the U.S. long bond had fully discounted the Fed tightening.
But the 30-year U.S. Treasury moved to a 6.97 percent yield at the close in New York overnight from 6.92 percent before.
Dealers said the U.S. market's move triggered early selling on the local market which forced jobbers to cut their long positions.
That, coupled with foreign selling, pushed yields more than 10 basis points higher on the day in generally thin volume trade.

Dealers said that on Thursday direction would be determined by the U.S. long bond's performance overnight. In early Wednesday New York trade, the T-bond had already visited the psychological 7.00 percent mark in the wake of a stronger-than-expected 1.5 percent in February.

The market would also look to the release of February consumer inflation data at 0900 GMT, which economists forecast will rise 0.45 percent month-on-month, and the possible release of February trade data.
Dealers said that on the day there had been talk that the trade balance would show a deficit rather than the 1.04 billion rand forecast by economists.

While some players suggested the figure had been leaked, others attributed the rumour to the fact that the data's release had been delayed. The market has been expecting the trade data to be released from the beginning of this week.
On the currency market, the rand's attempt to move below the 4.41 level on the back of exporter and offshore dollar selling was thwarted by importer and offshore buying.
The rand was last quoted at 4.4225/4255 against the dollar from 4.4165/4195 overnight.
"This morning we saw very good exporter dollars coming into the market and some from offshore which pushed it down to around 4.4120," a trader said.
"And from there we've seen importer demand and some demand from offshore and basically the rand has edged back to its opening," he said.
Trade on the day was described as thinnish, with big volumes moving through the market sporadically.
The rand was expected to hold a 4.41 to 4.43 range on Thursady, particularly as most players gone on holiday ahead of the upcoming long-weekend.
South African markets are closed on Friday and next Monday for the Easter holidays.
Money market rates remained within their recent ranges with three-month deposit rates quoted steady at 16.50 to 16.55 percent offered and the 90-day BA rate at between 15.90 to 16.10 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage edged up to 10.295 billion rand on Tuesday from 10.078 billion rand on Monday.
The Bond Exchange said that foreigners bought a net 359.56 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 173.86 million rand's worth on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes on Monday were pegged at 6.54 billion rand from 4.97 billion rand previously.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
